{{Quote|Baby banthas are quite cute, you know. A terrible shame to see one cut in half.&hellip;|[[Darth Vectivus]]|<ref name="Betrayal">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref>}}
'''Banthas''' were sturdy and easily domesticated [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]] used as beasts of burden that were found all over [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. The '''common bantha''', or '''''Bantha majorus''''', was the most commonly known species, with the other subspecies considered generally rare.

==Anatomy==
===Overview===
[[File:Bantha_Bull_and_Cow.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Bantha cow (female) and bull (male)]]
{{Quote|Banthas are filthy animals. I don't eat filthy animals.|[[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]]|audio=FilthyBanthas.flac|<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''</ref>}}
The bantha was one of the most adaptable [[Diet/Legends|herbivorous]] creatures in the galaxy and could be found on several worlds including [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. They were able to survive in almost any extremes of environment and could go without food or water for several weeks.<ref name="TEGtAS" /> They were highly intelligent and social,<ref name="Wildlife" /> but were considered [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]].<ref name="TEGtAS" /> Although bantha subspecies had diverged from their baseline ancestors, most shared similar characteristics. They were quadrupeds that were covered with long, shaggy fur and had large curved horns. A common bantha adult (''Bantha majorus'') was between two and three meters tall and could weigh up to 4,000 kilos. Their lifespan was between 80 and 100 years and they reached sexual maturity at the age of 20. Some sentient species had been known to ride banthas, such as [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]].<ref name="Wildlife" />

Bulls tended to be larger than the cows, and both [[Gender/Legends|genders]] grew a pair of spiral horns. Most female banthas achieved just a single spiral during their lifetimes, while a male could achieve two full spirals before its death.<ref name="Wildlife" /> The distinctive spiral horns of the bantha grew at the rate of a knob each year. Thickness and condition of the horns were an indication of the bantha's health and environment. Bulls fought each other by butting heads in ritual combat. The spirals on their horns could cause the pair to become entangled, which almost always meant death for both banthas, as the pair would soon collapse from exhaustion and eventually succumb to death by dehydration.<ref name="Wildlife" />

[[File:Bantha_tongue.jpg|thumb|250px|Bantha tongue anatomy]]

Banthas used their dexterous, sensitive tongue, as a sort of hand used in pulling up grass and shrubs from the ground. Also located on the tongue were breathing and scent spiracles. Male banthas also raised their tongue as a way to signal their readiness to mate.<ref name="Wildlife" />

Banthas traveled in herds of up to twenty-five individuals, led by the oldest, strongest female. A herd which grew too large was split, with the second oldest and strongest female taking the new herd. The gestation period was 30 months and the newborn's birth weight was about 50 kilograms.<ref name="Wildlife" />

Female banthas produced [[Blue milk/Legends|blue milk]]<ref name="Stay" /> from mammary glands that was consumed by [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] as a drink.<ref name="A New Hope" /> Bantha dung was another useful byproduct of the species, as it smoldered for a significant amount of time, and was used by the Tuskens as cooking fuel.<ref name="Out4">[[Star Wars (1998) 10|''Star Wars'' (1998) 10]]</ref>

Banthas had three-nailed hooves that were typically trimmed by their owners.<ref name="Out4" />

Banthas were harvested for their meat by workers or were put in [[Animal nursery|animal nurseries]] for long-term sustained harvesting on multiple worlds.<ref name="SW:GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

===Subspecies===
[[File:Feral_bantha.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Feral bantha from [[Talasea]]]]
There were at least three distinct subspecies found on the planet Tatooine: the ''common bantha'', the ''[[Dwarf bantha/Legends|dwarf bantha]]'', and the ''[[Dune bantha/Legends|dune bantha]]''.<ref name="Wildlife" /> Noted for their docility, the dwarf race (also referred to as "miniature banthas") made amiable pets, as in the case of [[Ebenn Q3 Baobab/Legends|Ebenn Q3 Baobab's]] companion, [[Nuke]].<ref name="GP&TG">[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']]</ref>

Another additional subspecies, the [[Kashyyyk bantha]], was suitably adapted for life on the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|homeworld]]<ref name="SWR 82 HE2" /> and the [[Kilian Bantha]] was adapted for living in the mountainous regions of [[Kilia IV/Legends|Kilia IV]].<ref name="Kilian" />

[[Feral bantha]]s were also found on [[Talasea]] where they developed an aggressive personality and roamed the forested world at will, attacking anything that crossed its path.<ref name="Databank" />

[[Swamp bantha]]s were brought to [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]] to help colonize the moon.<ref name="Gungan Frontier" />

==Banthas in the galaxy==
{{Quote|The Bantha is a gift from beyond whose meaning we have not yet begun to fathom! For when we do finally come to understand why the Bantha has been placed throughout the galaxy, we will achieve the Age of Bounty!|[[Hen]]|<ref name="TM">''[[Tatooine Manhunt]]''</ref>}}
Banthas could be found throughout the galaxy. It was said that the [[Age of Bounty]] would begin once people found out why the species had spread.<ref name="TM" /> The bantha was also domesticated on most worlds and were used for pulling heavy loads, transportation and even as war beasts. The meat and hide of the bantha were much sought-after.<ref name="Databank">{{DB|creature|bantha|bantha}}</ref> While the origins of the bantha were unknown, every world on which it existed laid claim to it as being its [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="AA">''[[Alien Anthology]]''</ref>

[[File:Bantha_herd.png|thumb|250px|A herd of banthas crossing the [[Dune Sea/Legends|Dune Sea]].]]
The bantha was an integral part of Tusken culture on Tatooine. When a Tusken Raider child reached the age of seven he or she was ceremonially presented with a bantha of the same age as a companion-for-life. The youth learned to care for the creature, and the two built a mystical bond. When the bantha reached maturity, the male Tusken Raider would [[Saddle/Legends|saddle]] his companion and ride it into the desert for adult initiation ceremonies.<ref name="Wildlife" />

When Tuskens married, the couple's banthas would also mate. Often, the resulting calf would be of the same gender as the Tusken child. The banthas of Tatooine were known to form deep bonds with the Tusken Raiders of the planet and often committed suicide if their riders were to die first. Banthas that died naturally were placed in vast graveyards, which other banthas treated with a kind of ceremonial reverence.<ref name="Wildlife" />

After the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Desert stormtrooper/Legends|sandtroopers]] began using banthas, in addition to the [[Dewback/Legends|Dewbacks]], as mounts. The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] officer [[Droma Ordo]] therefore led a mission to decrease the Bantha population around [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]] to reduce the number of Imperial patrols.<ref name="SWG:RBH">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=faction|Rebel|Rebel Bantha Hunt|Tatooine}}</ref> Ironically, the Rebels were using banthas to transport their supplies around the same time and Imperial [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Jasha]] also tasked a spacer to hunt down banthas near [[Bestine (city)/Legends|Bestine]].<ref name="SWG:IBH">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=faction|Imperial|Imperial Bantha Hunt|Tatooine}}</ref>

==The bantha in culture==
{{Quote|Spare us the bantha droppings.|[[Wes Janson/Legends|Wes Janson]] to [[Kapp Dendo]]|<ref name="Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: Battleground: Tatooine">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: Battleground: Tatooine]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Bantha_procession_TCG_Edge_of_Darkness.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] riding their bantha mounts in single file.]]
*[[Dim-U/Legends|Dim-U]] was a religious order based in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] that worshiped the bantha.<ref name="AA" />
*In one version of the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] sport of [[Phrenbi]], banthas were used as mounts.<ref name="TBSoS">''[[The Black Sands of Socorro]]''</ref>
*As an insult, people were referred to as "bantha fodder" ("bantha poodoo" in [[Huttese]]).<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>
*Banthas were the focus of a children's story called "[[The Little Lost Bantha Cub]]," which was the favorite bedtime story of [[Darth Caedus|Jacen]] and [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]].<ref name="Dark Apprentice">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref>
*[[Stuffed bantha]]s were popular toys among children in the galaxy. Wookiee [[Lumpawaroo/Legends|Lumpawaroo]] enjoyed his when he was young.<ref name="Tempest">''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]''</ref>
*Bantha meat was often eaten by Tatooine locals, in the form of [[Bantha steak/Legends|bantha steaks]], [[Bantha burger/Legends|bantha burgers]], and [[bantha rump]]. The [[Milk/Legends|milk]] of the female bantha was used to produce [[Bantha butter/Legends|bantha butter]]. Even the blood of the bantha was utilized to create [[Bantha-blood fizz/Legends|bantha-blood fizz]]. [[Bantha Breakfast Biscuit]]s were also believed to be derived from the bantha. The dining establishment [[BanthaQuik!]] served bantha in their [[Tusken Special]], one of their most popular meals.<ref name="DH">{{JournalCite|9|Death-Hunter}}</ref> The cookbook ''[[Essential Cooking Skills]]'' detailed how to best cook bantha meat.<ref name="SWG:ECS">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=item|ESSENTIAL COOKING SKILLS}}</ref>
*[[Bantha hide/Legends|Bantha hides]] were often used in making clothes or furniture.<ref name="LCatFoO">''[[Lando Calrissian and the Flamewind of Oseon]]''</ref>
*The phrase "grease the whole bantha" was used on [[Agamar/Legends|Agamar]] to indicate that total commitment was necessary.<ref name="Betrayal" />
*The phrase "wild bantha chase" referred to banthas.<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref>
*[[Chagrian/Legends|Chagrian]] [[Bouncer (occupation)/Legends|bouncer]] [[Burloo]] was nicknamed "Bantha."<ref name="BL">{{GamerCite|7|Bartyn's Landing (article)}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:BanthaCGI2.jpg|thumb|left|120px|CGI model for ''The Phantom Menace'']]
In the original version of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], the bantha was played by a trained [[Wikipedia:elephant|elephant]] named [[Mardji]] in a fur costume. In some cases, Mardji's trunk can be barely visible beneath the bantha costume. Re-releases and the [[prequel trilogy]] featured digital banthas. Their vocalizations were also done with a slowed-down bear's roar.<ref name="Drawing from the Present">{{SW|url=news/drawing-from-the-present-familiar-creatures-in-a-galaxy-far-far-away|text=Drawing from the Present: Familiar Creatures in a Galaxy Far, Far Away|int=Back from the Drawing Board|nolive=1}}</ref>

In [[1997]], [[Galoob]] released the first-ever licensed toy bantha as part of its Action Fleet line of micro-sized toys. In [[1998]], [[Kenner Products|Kenner]] made an action figure-scaled bantha. A reissue with different fur and figures came out in [[2007]]. For ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'', a toy bantha was created, although it was never released as a toy to the public.

Banthas appear in the video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]''. The player cannot control the bantha directly, but by hopping onto one using any other humanoid character, the bantha can be put to their use. Banthas in the game are extremely slow, and if you hop on one in the level in which they appear, Tusken Raiders come and attack the player.<ref name="LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy">''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref>

''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'' assign the rank "bantha fodder" to the player who dies the most on the battlefield.<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]''</ref><ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref>

The word "bantha" was capitalized in official publications up through at least the first edition of the [[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe|''Guide to the Star Wars Universe'']] in [[1984]].<ref name="A Guide to the Star Wars Universe">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]''</ref>
